quest.title: A Certain Stamp
quest.description: Iaune from the Maison Gestion is hard at work...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x3

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Thales, can I get my documents stamped now?

dialogues.speaker: Thales
dialogues.text: Yes! Of course you can. Did you bring the key? And please, sign here too.

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: I thought we wouldn't need to sign now that we've got the machine.

dialogues.speaker: Thales
dialogues.text: Well, about that... The machine must still be operated by someone, so you still have to sign in, don'cha? It's a guarantee.

dialogues.speaker: Thales
dialogues.text: But this machine is perfect for maintaining secrecy! Without a key, even I can't start it up!

dialogues.speaker: Thales
dialogues.text: Put the documents there, and make sure they are properly aligned. Then insert the key into the keyhole.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this that... automatic stamping machine? It looks really... ordinary...

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Like this? And just turn the key...

dialogues.speaker: Thales
dialogues.text: Wait a second! Just hold that pose, don't move! I'll take a picture.

response.speaker: Thales
response.text: When we first deployed these machines, Mr. Carsix specifically specified that we must use a Kamera to make a record of everyone that came to get documents stamped...

response.speaker: Thales
response.text: I need to move... Can't have this document in the frame.

response.speaker: Thales
response.text: Recently, someone said that there's going to be a new document promulgated here at the Maison Gestion, that specifically addresses secrets leaked through Kameras. I don't want to be the first one to be made an example of...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, let's go wait outside. If we're in the photo, maybe we'll get sucked into some kind of baloney involving "leaked secrets."

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Thales carefully takes a picture...

response.speaker: Thales
response.text: ...Okay, I've taken the photo. Please start up the machine.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: I turned the key already! Why isn't it responding?

response.speaker: Thales
response.text: That's impossible! I just repaired it. It can't be broken again already!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Thales begins to inspect the machine...

response.speaker: Thales
response.text: That's odd, there's nothing wrong with it...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Reinsert the key and try again?

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: Okay, here goes...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Iaune takes out the key, puts it back in, and the machine still doesn't move...

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: It's not working, Thales, think of something!

response.speaker: Thales
response.text: Maybe you didn't align the document properly? You need to fit the document to the markings, there are hidden trigger mechanisms inside.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Does the document have anything to do with the machine not starting?

response.speaker: Thales
response.text: Of course it does! Otherwise, how could the machine know there are documents waiting to be stamped? This is an automatic machine, after all, I'm not operating it manually!

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: Oh for the love of... Fine, fine! I'll make sure it's properly aligned with all the markings.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Iaune takes out the document and places it back. The machine still sits there, silently...

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: It's no good! It still isn't working.

response.speaker: Thales
response.text: How could this be? Though last time I gave it a little smack, and then it started working properly again.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Then I'll give it a whack.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: It appears we have no choice but to try it... Are we getting close to the point where we resort to prayer to try and fix it?

response.speaker: Thales
response.text: That's true, we can still pray, can't we?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Lightly tap the machine.)

response.speaker: Autostamper 3000
response.text: (The machine replies to you with complete silence...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Put a bit more oomph into this tap.)

response.speaker: Autostamper 3000
response.text: (The machine seems like it's too lazy to even care about your efforts.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Smack it so hard that its later iterations will feel it!)

response.speaker: Autostamper 3000
response.text: (The machine breaks its silence, and lets out a rusty, annoyed sound, as though a very sleepy person just fell out of bed...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! What's that sound? Don't tell Paimon the machine completely broke down!

response.speaker: Autostamper 3000
response.text: (...And then, as if the machine sleepily found its slippers and stumbled over to turn on the light, it begins to operate with a whirr and a clunk).

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: I—It's finally working...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The autostamper is well-worn, but it works slowly and methodically.\nWith several people on the brink of despair gazing at it intently, the machine slowly drops a stamp downward, with all the speed of an elderly Tent Tortoise climbing a cliff. The stamp, having taken its first step onto the paper, seems to stagger around on the document, before meandering slowly about, and finally settling down to rest. Finally, the machine shivers and shudders, and begins to slowly retract the stamp...

response.speaker: Thales
response.text: Haha, I TOLD you it would work!

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: I truly don't understand just what's so great about this machine. It's called "automatic," but it's far slower than just doing it by hand.

response.speaker: Thales
response.text: But it is perfect for maintaining confidentiality and secrecy! Look around! Even if we wanted to, we couldn't take the stamp out and use it for our own private purposes without permission!

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: Don't act so smug! What if the machine completely breaks down, and Mr. Carsix isn't here either? What then?

response.speaker: Thales
response.text: Hmm... Well, it'll still be okay. I have a backup key.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: To open up this machine?

response.speaker: Thales
response.text: No, to open up a box in Mr. Carsix's office. There's a backup stamp in there.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: ...Traveler, let's hurry up! We must bind and staple the document so we can deliver it to Mr. Difor.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: I can't wait to be free from this nightmare.

choices.text: Why do you want to take a photo?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Iaune!

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: Ah!? What!? Yes, yes, I finished, I finished writing!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's me! Did you finish writing it?

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: Oh, it's you... I... I must have fallen asleep. Sorry.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: Mr. Roialte and Mr. Semaine stayed with me half the night. With their guidance, I finally managed to finish the proposal.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: But I was just too tired, I thought I'd just close my eyes for a bit, I never thought I'd sleep until now...

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: I need to go find Mr. Thales first, and have him stamp this proposal with the official seal of the Maison Gestion, and then take the proposal to Mr. Difor for his stamp, and then we can begin officially printing it... and then we'll be done with this!

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: Yeah. In any case, I've heard that Mr. Thales has introduced a brand-new type of machine for affixing stamps. They say that it's convenient and made with confidentiality in mind, and that they plan to use it throughout the entire Maison Gestion.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: Take a look, Mr. Roialte even gave me a key! Every department must use this key to activate the stamping machine... Anyway, it all sounds pretty formal and official.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why don't you take another nap? It looks like you can barely walk straight.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, it's just getting a document stamped, and there's that... stamping machine to do it, there's no need to rush.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: No! We cannot afford any more delays. Let us go right away, like you said, it's only a stamp, it shouldn't take too much time.

choices.text: At least it's not as complicated as before.

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Okay! We have all the stamps, the document has been bound and stapled, and all that's left is to give it to Mr. Difor, and we'll finally be done!

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Today, I'm going to get a good night's sleep, and forget about all of this. Then I'll take a day off, and go find Estelle...

dialogues.speaker: Cornelia
dialogues.text: Mr. Iaune, do you have a moment?

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Yes, what is it? No way did the reimbursement get approved so quickly.

dialogues.speaker: Cornelia
dialogues.text: That it did not, but... Monsieur Neuvillette sent someone to me, and had me come ask you... Why are you expensing a single keycap, and not an entire typewriter?

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: Because... well, because a single keycap fell off, that's all! Why would I need to expense an entire new typewriter?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know, that does make sense.

dialogues.speaker: Cornelia
dialogues.text: Perhaps, but our list of items eligible for reimbursement includes typewriters, not individual keycaps. As such, keycaps are a brand-new payment item.

dialogues.speaker: Cornelia
dialogues.text: Therefore, you must submit a written document to Monsieur Neuvillette, and explain in detail why you are expensing that single keycap...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why does it feel like some kind of bad joke, and not actual government business...

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: So, you want me to... to write a separate report to the Chief Justice, explaining how I lost a single keycap?

response.speaker: Cornelia
response.text: The Maison Cardinalice said that it was a request from Monsieur Neuvillette himself.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: As if! The Maison Cardinalice says everything is "a request from Monsieur Neuvillette himself"!

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: But no one dares test the waters and see if that's actually the truth. Come now, Iaune, calm down and listen to me.

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: As a Gestionnaire of the Maison Gestion, orders from the Chief Justice are an imperative, carrying the full weight of the administration. Simply put, you have no choice but to write it.

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: Not that this is a bad thing, you know! You can use this chance to show off your handwriting to him. Not everyone gets a chance to make a separate report to him!

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: But, I...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Uh-oh...

response.speaker: Gattineo
response.text: Hello! Friends, good news! We just caught someone leaking secrets with a Kamera red-handed! A sterling example of negative behavior that we shall conclude in the proposal.

response.speaker: Gattineo
response.text: And as for this criminal who knew the law yet knowingly violated it, is in fact the very person who reminded everyone not to use Kameras lest they expose secrets, Mr. Carsix.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Him...! It's because of him that Iaune was up all night writing the proposal! And now he's been caught breaking the rules first, no less!

response.speaker: Gattineo
response.text: He used a Kamera to take multiple photos of his office, and then distributed them to reporters.

response.speaker: Gattineo
response.text: One of the photos included his own minutes from meetings. And the public has now discovered, the contents of the minutes are wildly different from what he said in his previous speeches.

response.speaker: Gattineo
response.text: Rumors are swirling like mad, and it appears that Mr. Carsix's office is about to become the biggest joke in Fontaine... again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait a minute! What do the minutes have to do with the speech?

response.speaker: Gattineo
response.text: Almost all of the contents of the speech were agreed upon in the meetings recorded by those minutes. Of course they're related.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So why are they so different?

response.speaker: Gattineo
response.text: Oh, that's actually quite normal. The purpose of the meetings and the minutes is to tell us exactly what content cannot appear in the speech.

response.speaker: Gattineo
response.text: Carsix himself hasn't got the foggiest notion of what he's going to say, and doesn't even have his own ideas. He is completely reliant on being reminded by his subordinates.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: Wait, so where is Mr. Carsix now?

response.speaker: Gattineo
response.text: He's awaiting investigation in my office. After all, not only did he leak secret documents, but he also caused quite the storm in the city... I think he may have to stay in there awhile.

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: But what about my document!? I finished writing it, it's all stamped up and ready and... I... *cough* *cough* *cough*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: H—Hey now, it's okay, you wrote it, it'll get sent out eventually.

choices.text: It wasn't a waste, calm down.

response.speaker: Semaine
response.text: Iaune! Iaune, are you there?

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: Mr. Semaine, you're finally here! Please, help me think of something!

response.speaker: Semaine
response.text: Don't talk about that now! Your keycap, have you already expensed it?

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: You think? I even have to write a report to Monsieur Neuvillette himself about it.

response.speaker: Semaine
response.text: Oh... Drat.

response.speaker: Semaine
response.text: Take a look. Is this that keycap?

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: You... Where did you find it?

response.speaker: Semaine
response.text: It was under my desk. Just as the cleaning staff was sweeping, they accidentally swept it over. Someone saw it and put it on my desk.

response.speaker: Semaine
response.text: I thought it was a keycap from my own typewriter at first, so I put it away. But today, I took a look and... I realized my typewriter wasn't missing a single keycap, so...

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: This nightmare... when will it end...

response.speaker: Iaune
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, what, really, is the meaning behind my work...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Iaune falls to the ground in a faint...

response.speaker: Crowd
response.text: Iaune? Iaune!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Iaune is rushed to the doctor...

response.speaker: Semaine
response.text: Ah, this is all my fault! If only I'd found the keycap earlier, things wouldn't have turned out like this.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How is this issue about the keycap, hello!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! Everything's a complete mess. Iaune didn't even know what to do!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Gattineo and Difor have also just vanished... What's going on with these guys, anyway?

choices.text: Iaune cares about the meaning of his work.

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: *sigh* That kid's always thinking about those sorts of things.

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: "The point of work"... Such a grand topic can't be easily explained in just a few words.

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: You'll only heap more pressure on yourself by constantly worrying about such issues.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, do you know the answer, then?

response.speaker: Semaine
response.text: No. I've never even considered it. I just work.

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: As for me... While I do think about it now and then, I have my own way to deal with stress.

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: If you really want to find the answer, perhaps we could find some time to talk more.

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: But right now, I've got to buy some fruit and go see Iaune.

response.speaker: Semaine
response.text: Now that's the main matter, and no mistake. I'm also going to go help Iaune apply for sick leave. He really needs to rest.

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: Great, we each have our tasks. That's the way to get things done.

response.speaker: Roialte
response.text: #We'll see you later then, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Semaine
response.text: Huh? That's weird... Where did I put that sick leave form...?

choices.text: Iaune doesn't know what the point of his work is.
Please, relax, there's always a way.

dialogues.speaker: Thales
dialogues.text: This machine sure is hard to use... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Iaune
dialogues.text: The wording here needs to be reconsidered... Now, what's the best way to phrase it...?
